sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 2026 lecture-note manuscript (781 KB PDF) from the author's Aalto page and inspected the extracted full text. Read Chapter 3 §§3.1-3.4 in full: the dilation argument and the forced exponent (p. 61), the generalized Holder estimate (Lemma 3.2), the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev theorem with its product estimates for p=1 and its power/Holder reduction and density passage for 1<p<n (Theorem 3.3 and Remarks 3.4), the consequences for W_0^{1,p} and open sets (Corollaries 3.5-3.6), the Poincare inequality for W_0^{1,p} on bounded sets with its one-direction product proof (Theorem 3.10 and Remark 3.11), the cube Poincare and Sobolev-Poincare inequalities (Theorems 3.12-3.13, Remarks 3.14-3.16, Theorem 3.17, Remark 3.20), Morrey's theorem with the cube-oscillation proof and the remarks on representatives (Theorem 3.23, Remarks 3.25), the differentiability theorem for p>n (Theorem 3.28) and the Lipschitz/W^{1,\infty} theorem (Theorem 3.31). Read Chapter 5 §5.3 (Lemma 5.15, Lemma 5.22, Remark 5.23, Theorems 5.24-5.28) in full, and Chapter 5 §5.9 (Definition 5.31, Remarks 5.32, the complete chain construction in the proof of Theorem 5.33, Example 5.34). Also read the extension-domain statement Theorem 3.47 and its compactness proof (Chapter 3 §3.6).
